title: Product listings expose both a sample price and zero-price items
observation: The captured Glucare Plus product page text presents a 1-package listing at 9,000 VND and other product listings at 0 VND in the same product section.

impact.user: A self-purchaser or adult child cannot tell from the captured state whether zero is a real price, unavailable price, or placeholder.
impact.business: Ambiguous price presentation can interrupt purchase confidence.

suggested_direction: Replace zero-price merchandising states with an explicit availability or contact-for-price label and keep package/price meaning consistent.
unknowns: The capture does not establish inventory, configuration, or backend pricing state.
persona_impact: Both an older self-purchaser and an adult child buying for a parent need an unambiguous package and payable price before proceeding.
limitations: Cart mutation and checkout were not performed; no payable total was observed.

title: Health and safety claims appear without an identifiable supporting-document route in the captured product state
observation: The captured Glucare Plus page states that it is suitable for people with diabetes, uses “Công thức y khoa ADDP”, and safely supports blood-glucose control; the captured link set exposes an ingredient anchor but no visible link labelled as a study, declaration, certification, or supporting document.

impact.user: A skeptical adult child cannot trace these high-stakes claims to supporting material from the captured product state.
impact.business: Unverifiable claim presentation can reduce trust for a health-related purchase.
impact.seo: Clear source and evidence links can improve entity and claim context.

suggested_direction: Place clearly labelled public supporting sources, product declarations, and appropriate-use boundaries next to the relevant claims.
unknowns: No judgment is made about medical validity, effectiveness, document authenticity, certification authenticity, or individual suitability.
A source may exist outside the captured page or selected scope.
persona_impact: An adult child researching for a parent needs to distinguish marketing claims from evidence shown or linked by the site.
limitations: Conclusion is limited to links and text in the captured browser state.

title: Product section mixes 9,000 VND and zero-price listings
observation: The captured product state lists a 1-package Glucare Plus item at 9,000 VND while other product cards in the same section expose 0 VND prices.

impact.user: The researcher cannot determine the actual package and purchase price for the zero-price items.
impact.business: Inconsistent visible price information weakens comparison and purchase confidence.

suggested_direction: Use explicit, consistent package and price labels; replace zero placeholders with a meaningful availability state.
unknowns: The capture does not establish backend price configuration or whether every listing represents the same package.
persona_impact: An adult child comparing options for a parent needs consistent product/package/price information.
limitations: No cart or checkout total was observed.

title: Mobile icon links lack accessible names
observation: The mobile accessibility artifact reports serious link-name failures for the cart, home, search, mobile-cart, and account icon links because the focusable elements have no discernible accessible text or ARIA label.

impact.user: Icon-only controls are harder to identify with assistive technology and provide weak explicit labeling for users with limited confidence.
impact.business: Unclear navigation and cart controls can obstruct product and purchase tasks.

suggested_direction: Give each icon control a localized accessible name and retain a clear visible or programmatic label across mobile states.
unknowns: The audit did not conduct a human screen-reader session.
persona_impact: A mobile user should not have to infer search, cart, account, or home actions from icon shape alone.
limitations: Impact is based on deterministic axe output and captured DOM, not a human assistive-technology test.

title: Product-price text fails automated contrast checks on mobile
observation: The mobile accessibility artifact reports serious color-contrast failures for product-price text, including gold text at 2.77:1 on the light background and gray text at 2.45:1, below the stated 3:1 or 4.5:1 thresholds.

impact.user: Low-contrast price text can be difficult to read, especially for visitors with reduced contrast sensitivity.
impact.business: Price legibility affects product comparison and confidence.
impact.technical: Rendered foreground/background combinations fail automated contrast rules.

suggested_direction: Adjust price colors or backgrounds so rendered text meets the applicable WCAG contrast ratio in every product-card state.
unknowns: Automated contrast results should be confirmed against final design tokens and states.
persona_impact: Middle-aged and older visitors need price information that remains legible without zoom or unusually high visual effort.
limitations: The result applies to the captured mobile rendering and does not measure individual visual ability.

title: The homepage hero does not show a principal product
observation: The stabilized desktop and mobile first-view captures show the ADDP logo, the message "Chăm sóc từ giá trị thiện lành", the headline "Sức Khỏe Bền Vững Khởi Nguồn Từ Tâm", an older couple, supporting copy, and the actions "Khám phá ngay" and "Tư vấn miễn phí". No product package or named principal product is visible in either captured first viewport. REQ-004 calls for the first viewport to combine a core message, a principal-product image, and a large clear CTA; the message and actions are present, while the product-image element is absent from the captured state.

impact.user: A first-time visitor can understand the care-oriented brand message, but must continue down the page before seeing what ADDP sells. This adds orientation work for an older or middle-aged self-purchaser and for an adult child quickly assessing a product for a parent.
impact.business: The first viewport does not immediately connect the brand promise to a specific purchasable product, weakening product discovery at the earliest decision point.

suggested_direction: Keep the current human, reassuring message, but add a clearly identifiable principal-product packshot or product grouping within the first desktop and mobile viewport and preserve an obvious route to that product.
unknowns: Whether another timed or carousel state shows a product before user interaction.
Whether the hero is intended to prioritize corporate positioning over immediate product orientation.
specialist_interpretation: The existing headline, supportive imagery, and two visible actions are positive orientation signals. Within the ADDP customer context, product identification is still a necessary part of first-view confidence because the researcher or purchaser may differ from the eventual product user.
limitations: This visual conclusion is limited to the saved stabilized viewport state at 1440x1000 and 390x1000; animation was frozen after stabilization, and the homepage had a material initial-to-stabilized difference.
The render remained partial with residual resource/decode failures, so this finding does not claim that every possible hero state lacks product imagery.
The first-time and high-intent journey interaction failures were excluded because they may be audit-induced and do not establish a site defect.

title: Mobile typography falls below the checklist's reading-size targets
observation: The Glucare mobile DOM records its hero heading at 23.4px and several ingredient headings at 15.5px. Those measured examples are below the checklist targets of 28–32px for mobile headings and 16px for body text. The examples support a product-page typography concern; no exhaustive text inventory is claimed.

impact.user: Small supporting copy and undersized headings increase reading effort on a phone, particularly for visitors with ordinary age-related vision changes or limited tolerance for dense health-product information.
impact.business: Visitors may scan past trust details, ingredient labels, or product distinctions that support confidence and purchase decisions.

suggested_direction: Raise mobile body and supporting text to at least 16px, bring primary and section headings into the 28-32px range where practical, and use 1.5-1.6 line height for reading copy while preserving the current responsive width behavior.
unknowns: The DOM text sampler does not inventory every visible text node, so the finding identifies evidenced examples rather than an exhaustive count.
User browser zoom, operating-system text scaling, and device pixel density were not varied.
specialist_interpretation: The three inspected mobile layouts fit their recorded viewport widths without horizontal overflow, which is positive. The remaining legibility burden comes from text sizing and line spacing rather than a broken responsive width in these captures.
limitations: Measurements come from the saved 390-400px mobile DOM captures only.
All relevant page collections remained partial; Glucare had pending images, and all three pages recorded residual resource/decode failures.
No claim is made about individual medical suitability or comprehension of the health statements.

title: Homepage hero actions are less prominent and less thumb-friendly than product-page CTAs
observation: In the stabilized mobile homepage DOM, "Khám phá ngay" measures about 142.5x38.2px and "Tư vấn miễn phí" about 134.6x32px; both use 13.5px text and appear as lightweight text/icon actions in the stabilized screenshot. By comparison, the saved mobile product pages show a 358x54.3px Glucare purchase action and a 303.6x54.4px Dovital purchase action as prominent filled controls. The homepage consultation action therefore does not match REQ-005's request for a large, rounded, strongly contrasting mobile action that is easy to press with a thumb, although the product-page purchase actions provide a positive implementation pattern.

impact.user: The two homepage choices are visible, but their smaller height and lighter button affordance demand more precision and provide less obvious prioritization for a phone user with ordinary or limited digital confidence.
impact.business: The homepage gives less visual emphasis to exploration and consultation than the product pages give to purchase, which may reduce progression from the first brand encounter.

suggested_direction: Apply the product pages' successful mobile CTA pattern to the homepage hero: use a clearly filled, rounded primary action with at least a 44px hit height, retain a distinct secondary consultation action, and keep both labels explicit.
unknowns: No touch-usability study was performed, so the impact is based on measured hit areas and visible affordance.
The saved evidence does not establish which of the two homepage actions is intended to be primary.
specialist_interpretation: The contrast with the two product pages is useful positive evidence: ADDP already uses large mobile purchase controls in the same site experience, so the homepage inconsistency is visible to both self-purchasers and adult-child researchers.
limitations: The comparison uses stabilized screenshots and computed rectangles at one mobile viewport per page.
The homepage had a material initial-to-stabilized visual difference, so only the stabilized state supports this finding.
No click outcome is claimed; persona journey navigation errors were excluded as possible audit-induced behavior.

title: Shared mobile utility navigation creates precision and assistive-technology barriers
observation: On the captured Glucare mobile page, the Search and Cart links measure 35×35px. The mobile accessibility scan reports serious link-name failures for cart, home, search, mobile-cart, and account icons and nested focusable controls in the menu, account and settings tab-like items. This supports a shared mobile navigation concern from the captured page.

impact.user: The 35px icon targets require more precise tapping, while unnamed and nested controls make the same navigation harder to identify or operate with a screen reader or keyboard. This affects recovery and wayfinding across the homepage and product journey.
impact.business: Search, account access, and cart access are recurring commerce routes; friction in the shared controls can interrupt product discovery and purchase progression on every inspected core page.
impact.technical: The saved accessibility scans identify missing accessible names, invalid child relationships for the tablist, and nested interactive descendants in the shared navigation semantics.

suggested_direction: Give every utility control a clear programmatic name and, where space permits, a visible text label; enlarge touch areas to at least 44x44px without reducing icon clarity; and expose each mobile navigation choice as one focusable control with valid parent/child roles and state attributes.
unknowns: Keyboard order and spoken screen-reader output were not manually tested.
The evidence does not measure accidental-tap frequency in real use.
specialist_interpretation: The header and fixed bottom bar make these utilities easy to find visually, which is positive. The present icon-only treatment and semantic failures still impose avoidable precision and interpretation demands for mobile visitors and assistive-technology users.
limitations: The finding uses direct DOM rectangles and axe results from the saved mobile states; it does not claim that every assistive technology reacts identically.
The page collections were partial, but the controls were present, visible, and independently measured in the stabilized DOM and screenshot evidence.
No implementation cause is inferred.

title: Low-contrast supporting text and prices weaken scanability
observation: On the captured Glucare mobile page, sampled gold product-price text is reported at 2.86:1 against the applicable 4.5:1 expectation. This is an observed low-contrast price example; other product and homepage color combinations are not asserted here.

impact.user: Visitors with reduced contrast sensitivity may miss section orientation labels or struggle to read price information while scanning product choices, even though the main headings and primary CTAs remain easier to see.
impact.business: Harder-to-read prices and supporting labels can weaken product comparison and confidence during research or purchase consideration.

suggested_direction: Darken the gray, gold, and orange text colors or adjust their backgrounds so normal-size text reaches at least 4.5:1 and large bold text reaches at least 3:1, then recheck the exact rendered combinations on desktop and mobile.
unknowns: The automated scan samples rendered color combinations but does not quantify every text element on the pages.
Display calibration, ambient light, and user contrast settings were not varied.
specialist_interpretation: The affected content includes orientation cues and prices that matter to both an older or middle-aged self-purchaser and an adult child comparing options for a parent. The evidence supports a legibility issue only; it does not establish price correctness or product suitability.
limitations: The full-page visual review used only stabilized screenshots; provisional screenshots were excluded.
The captures remained partial with residual resource/decode failures, but the contrast values come from rendered elements that were present in the stabilized DOM.
No inference is made about the validity of health claims, certifications, or individual suitability.

title: The two homepage hero CTAs share a non-directional hash target
observation: In the stabilized desktop and mobile DOM evidence, the visible hero actions "Khám phá ngay" and "Tư vấn miễn phí" both resolve to https://addp.vn/#. The stabilized rendered HTML records both anchors as href="#". The two labels are visible and distinguish product discovery from consultation, but the saved anchors do not encode distinct destinations for those actions.

impact.user: A first-time visitor choosing between exploration and advice is not given a destination-specific route by either primary hero action.
impact.business: The highest-visibility conversion choices do not provide a direct, differentiated handoff to a product or consultation destination in the saved page state.
impact.technical: Both saved anchor targets point to the same page fragment target.

suggested_direction: Give each hero action a concrete, distinct destination: a principal-product or product-selection route for discovery and the consultation form or support route for advice. Retain the differentiated labels and verify the resulting destinations in read-only QA.
unknowns: The saved evidence does not establish whether runtime event handlers supplement the hash anchors in other sessions.
The intended destination for each hero action is not stated in the captured page.
specialist_interpretation: For both a self-purchaser and an adult child researching for a parent, the hero presents two useful intents but does not expose where either choice will lead. This adds uncertainty at the first conversion decision without negating the clear mission copy and visible action labels.
limitations: This conclusion is limited to the saved stabilized rendered HTML and DOM state.
Audit-induced journey navigation errors were excluded and are not treated as website defects.
No form submission, cart mutation, or other state-changing interaction was performed.

title: The homepage hero does not show a principal product
observation: The stabilized first viewport on desktop and mobile shows the ADDP mission message, supporting copy, the two hero actions, and a photograph of an older couple. No named or packaged principal product is visible in that hero. Principal product imagery and links for Glucare Plus, Viên An Đường, and Dovital appear farther down the stabilized full-page captures.

impact.user: A first-time visitor can understand the brand promise but cannot identify a principal product from the initial viewport.
impact.business: The opening screen delays the connection between the brand message and the products the site is trying to sell.

suggested_direction: Add a clearly named principal product or product group, with recognizable packaging, to the hero while preserving the current mission message and human imagery. Connect the adjacent discovery CTA to that product route.
unknowns: The evidence does not state which principal product should lead the homepage hero.
The audit does not measure whether the current human image or a product-led variant converts better.
specialist_interpretation: The current hero supports emotional reassurance for middle-aged and older users, but an adult child or self-purchaser must scroll before learning which concrete ADDP product is being offered. The finding concerns product visibility only and does not assess the identity or suitability of the people pictured.
limitations: The page-level render status is partial because residual resource failures were recorded; the finding relies only on the stabilized screenshots supplied for visual interpretation.
The full-page evidence confirms that principal product routes exist lower on the homepage.
No inference is made about image authenticity, medical value, or individual product suitability.

title: Purchase CTAs appear before any visible price on both principal product pages
observation: On the stabilized Glucare Plus page, the purchase CTA is visible in the first viewport while the first price-bearing product sample appears farther down the captured page. The captured mobile CTA begins around y=484 px, while the first price-bearing product sample appears around y=1,744 px; the desktop capture shows the same sequence, with the price-bearing sample below the first viewport.

impact.user: A high-intent self-purchaser or adult child cannot evaluate the advertised offer price before choosing the prominent purchase action.
impact.business: Price uncertainty is introduced at the strongest buying prompt on two critical product routes, increasing the amount of exploration needed before a purchase decision.

suggested_direction: Place the current price, package or quantity, and any promotion terms beside each primary hero CTA. If the CTA jumps to multiple offer cards, state that clearly and summarize the starting price or available package range before the action.
unknowns: The captured heroes do not identify which downstream package each primary CTA is intended to represent.
The evidence does not establish promotion duration or eligibility.
specialist_interpretation: The product identity and primary action are strong, especially on mobile, but both purchase audiences must act or scroll without first seeing the commercial terms. This is a price-visibility issue; it does not question the products' health claims or suitability.
limitations: Price-bearing product cards are present farther down both pages and are preserved as positive evidence.
The finding is based on stabilized screenshots and captured element coordinates, not on an order attempt.
No cart, checkout, payment, account, or form mutation was performed.

title: Purchasable product cards display 0,00 ₫ beside paid alternatives
observation: The captured Glucare Plus page shows a related Glucare Plus product card at 0,00 ₫ with an add-to-cart control beside a 9.000,00 ₫ sachet and a 560.000,00 ₫ item. The visible cards therefore show inconsistent prices in the same product section; the reason for the zero-price state is unknown.

impact.user: A purchaser cannot tell from the cards whether 0,00 ₫ means free, unavailable, price on request, or another offer state, especially when similar paid alternatives are adjacent.
impact.business: Ambiguous zero-price offers can weaken price confidence and interrupt product comparison at the add-to-cart decision.

suggested_direction: Replace each unexplained 0,00 ₫ display with the actual public price or an explicit customer-facing state such as unavailable, contact for price, or free sample with conditions. Differentiate similarly named packages by quantity and contents before the add-to-cart control.
unknowns: The saved public evidence does not establish the intended commercial state of either zero-price item.
The amount that would be charged after cart mutation is unknown because cart mutation was prohibited.
specialist_interpretation: This ambiguity affects both an older self-purchaser and an adult child comparing products for a parent because the displayed amount conflicts with the surrounding paid offer context. The finding reports only the public display and makes no claim about backend price state.
limitations: No add-to-cart, cart, checkout, order, or payment action was executed.
The evidence cannot determine whether the zero-price items are intentionally free, placeholders, unavailable, or incorrectly configured.
No inference is made about backend state or the eventual transaction amount.

title: Homepage presents a coherent ADDP promise, product family, and human imagery
observation: The stabilized desktop and mobile homepage captures show the ADDP Pharmacy logo, a navy-and-white visual system with warm yellow accents, the promise "Chăm sóc từ giá trị thiện lành / Sức Khỏe Bền Vững Khởi Nguồn Từ Tâm," an older couple in the hero, multiple real-person care images, a panel naming GLUCARE PLUS, VIÊN AN ĐƯỜNG, and DOVITAL, and a testimonial section with names and portraits.

impact.user: This gives both an older or middle-aged self-purchaser and an adult child researching for a parent immediate cues about the company promise, intended care context, principal product lines, and available human support.
impact.business: The homepage creates a recognizable ADDP brand frame and gives the three priority product lines visible portfolio context.

suggested_direction: Preserve the combination of clear ADDP ownership, plain-language promise, real-person imagery, named product family, and support cues as other pages are refined.
unknowns: The saved evidence does not establish whether the testimonial identities or statements are independently verified.
The Viên An Đường destination was not collected as a product-detail page in this run, so its downstream presentation cannot be assessed.
specialist_interpretation: This is positive brand evidence. The imagery and copy connect ADDP with care, clarity, and accompaniment without relying only on product packs; that is useful for a self-purchaser and for an adult child deciding whether the company feels understandable and supportive.
limitations: The screenshots are stabilized but the run remained partial because of residual resource/decode failures. This finding records visible presentation only and does not validate testimonials, health claims, certifications, or product suitability.

title: Product landing pages fragment the ADDP visual identity
observation: The captured Glucare Plus product page uses a cream, brown and gold palette across its main sections, while the captured ADDP homepage uses navy, white and warm yellow accents. The shared logo and global header remain visible on both pages, but the main Glucare product sections do not repeat the homepage palette prominently.

impact.user: Moving from the homepage into different products can feel like entering separate campaign sites, increasing the effort required to recognize that the same company stands behind each offer.
impact.business: The visual split weakens portfolio coherence and reduces the transfer of trust built on the ADDP homepage to individual product propositions.

suggested_direction: Define a shared ADDP product-page frame using recurring navy brand anchors, typography, trust modules, and portfolio cues, while retaining controlled product-specific accent colors for Glucare Plus and Dovital.
unknowns: No separate brand-standards document or source logo palette was included in the allowed inputs; consistency was assessed from the checklist and rendered pages.
The Viên An Đường product page was not present in the collected inventory, so the three-product system could not be compared in full.
specialist_interpretation: For both a self-purchaser and an adult child comparing products for a parent, consistent ADDP ownership matters because trust must carry from company to product. The current pages show product personality clearly, but ADDP's portfolio identity becomes much less dominant inside the two captured product experiences.
limitations: This is a visual-consistency assessment of stabilized captures. It does not assert a source-level cause, and the partial render status means unseen or unresolved assets may affect some lower-page details.

title: Visible safety and standards claims lack identifiable proof
observation: The homepage trust strip states "Chứng nhận an toàn" and "Sản phẩm đạt tiêu chuẩn chất lượng và an toàn" beside a generic badge icon, but the stabilized homepage evidence does not show a named certificate, standard identifier, issuer, or public document. The separate company page introduces a "Tiêu chuẩn" section while its four intended standard visuals render as pale generic placeholder tiles; the rendered HTML lists those images with empty alternative text.

impact.user: A skeptical buyer researching for a parent can see that safety and standards are asserted but cannot identify what credential or standard the visible claim refers to, limiting informed trust.
impact.business: Generic claims and placeholder-like standards imagery reduce the credibility value that visible certification or quality evidence could provide at a key decision point.

suggested_direction: Replace generic proof cues with readable, named credential or standard details, contextual captions, and public supporting documents where the company can substantiate them; ensure the company-page visuals render as identifiable evidence rather than placeholders.
unknowns: The run does not establish whether supporting certificates or documents exist elsewhere outside the collected paths.
Whether the pale tiles are source images or render-time fallbacks is unknown; no implementation cause is asserted.
The authenticity or validity of any certificate, standard, or health claim was not assessed.
specialist_interpretation: For an older or middle-aged buyer, the short trust strip is easy to scan, but it remains an assertion. For an adult child doing deeper diligence, the company page is the natural place to verify the claim, and the visible standards area does not provide identifiable evidence in this run.
limitations: This finding is limited to what is visibly named or rendered in the saved homepage and company-page evidence. It does not infer certification authenticity, health validity, backend state, or the absence of documents beyond the collected scope.

title: Company page opens with an untranslated title and oversized mobile void
observation: The stabilized company page displays the English H1 "About us" above otherwise Vietnamese company content. In the stabilized mobile viewport, a large blank vertical region separates the header from the breadcrumb and that English H1 before the Vietnamese heading "CHÀO MỪNG BẠN ĐẾN VỚI DƯỢC PHẨM ADDP."

impact.user: The mixed-language title and long empty opening make the company-information page feel less finished and delay the identity content, especially for a phone visitor with limited digital confidence.
impact.business: The presentation weakens the polish of the page most likely to be used to verify who ADDP is and what it stands for.

suggested_direction: Use a Vietnamese page title consistent with the rest of the page and tighten the mobile opening so the company identity and introductory content appear directly below the header and breadcrumb.
unknowns: The saved evidence does not determine whether the blank region is intentional spacing, an invisible asset, or another rendering condition.
specialist_interpretation: The company page is a trust destination for both first-time visitors and adult children researching for a parent. Language and layout polish carry disproportionate weight here because the page is expected to confirm company identity and credibility.
limitations: The observation is based on stabilized desktop and mobile evidence and the indexed rendered HTML. No probable implementation cause is offered.

title: Product page does not present a direct FAQ block in the captured content
observation: The captured Glucare Plus product page includes product claims, ingredient sections, usage steps and offers, but its visible heading and text extract contains no FAQ or question-and-answer block.

impact.user: A buyer researching for a parent may not find direct answers to appropriate use, interactions or limits at the product decision point.
impact.business: Unanswered purchase questions can prevent informed decisions.
impact.seo: A structured question-and-answer section can improve direct answer extraction.

suggested_direction: Add evidence-grounded FAQ answers with explicit boundaries and reviewed sources beside the product information.
unknowns: Assessment is limited to captured page text and headings; content may change after this observation.
specialist_interpretation: The captured Glucare Plus product page includes product claims, ingredient sections, usage steps and offers, but its visible heading and text extract contains no FAQ or question-and-answer block.
limitations: Assessment is limited to captured page text and headings; content may change after this observation.

title: Product claims about blood-glucose support are shown without a linked evidence source in the captured state
observation: The product page text says the product is usable by people with diabetes and describes support for maintaining or safely controlling blood glucose; the captured visible links include an ingredient anchor but no link to a study, public declaration or claim source.

impact.user: An adult child cannot distinguish the stated health claim from supporting material within the captured product state.
impact.business: Health-related claims without visible support may weaken trust.
impact.seo: Claim context and attributable sources are absent from the captured linked material.

suggested_direction: Place reviewable public sources and appropriate-use boundaries next to each health-related claim.
unknowns: No conclusion about validity, clinical effectiveness, certification or document authenticity, or individual suitability.
specialist_interpretation: The product page text says the product is usable by people with diabetes and describes support for maintaining or safely controlling blood glucose; the captured visible links include an ingredient anchor but no link to a study, public declaration or claim source.
limitations: No conclusion about validity, clinical effectiveness, certification or document authenticity, or individual suitability.

title: Product page retains a generic meta description
observation: The rendered SEO artifact records the Glucare Plus page meta description as “Default Description” on both desktop and mobile.

impact.user: Search previews may not describe the specific product page.
impact.business: A generic snippet may reduce relevance for product searches.
impact.seo: The product URL has a non-specific description.

suggested_direction: Write a unique accurate description for the product page and verify it in the rendered document.
unknowns: Search-result appearance and ranking impact were not measured.
specialist_interpretation: The rendered SEO artifact records the Glucare Plus page meta description as “Default Description” on both desktop and mobile.
limitations: Search-result appearance and ranking impact were not measured.

title: Both discovered sitemap URLs returned HTTP 404 during the audit
observation: Discovery recorded HTTP 404 for both https://addp.vn/pub/sitemap.xml and https://addp.vn/sitemap.xml.

impact.business: A crawler may not discover an XML sitemap through these advertised URLs.
impact.seo: The robots file advertises a sitemap URL that returned 404; the alternate root sitemap URL also returned 404.
impact.technical: Both observed sitemap endpoints returned HTTP 404.

suggested_direction: Publish a valid sitemap at the advertised URL and verify its response and submitted URL set.
unknowns: The audit did not access Search Console or verify other sitemap locations.
specialist_interpretation: Discovery recorded HTTP 404 for both https://addp.vn/pub/sitemap.xml and https://addp.vn/sitemap.xml.
limitations: The audit did not access Search Console or verify other sitemap locations.

title: Homepage and product pages expose no JSON-LD in the captured desktop/mobile pages
observation: The indexed JSON-LD evidence artifacts contain empty arrays for the homepage and captured Glucare Plus desktop and mobile pages; no Organization, Product or FAQPage JSON-LD item was recorded in these captures.

impact.business: Machine-readable entity and product information is not present in these captured pages.
impact.seo: Requested structured entity, product and FAQ data is absent from the observed pages.
impact.technical: The JSON-LD collector returned empty arrays for sampled pages.

suggested_direction: Add validated Organization markup and accurate Product and FAQPage markup where the corresponding visible content exists.
unknowns: Finding is limited to sampled pages and JSON-LD; other structured-data formats were not assessed here.
specialist_interpretation: The indexed JSON-LD evidence artifacts contain empty arrays for the homepage and captured Glucare Plus desktop and mobile pages; no Organization, Product or FAQPage JSON-LD item was recorded in these captures.
limitations: Finding is limited to sampled pages and JSON-LD; other structured-data formats were not assessed here.

title: Required Organization and Product JSON-LD was not present in sampled pages
observation: The captured JSON-LD artifacts are empty arrays on the homepage and Glucare Plus product page at desktop and mobile viewports.

impact.business: Search and assistant systems lack the requested structured product and organization declarations in these samples.
impact.seo: Organization and Product JSON-LD required by the checklist was not observed.
impact.technical: No JSON-LD object was returned by the sampled page collectors.

suggested_direction: Add structured data that matches visible, verifiable page content and validate it against current parsers.
unknowns: Only JSON-LD was tested; this does not rule out other structured data formats.
specialist_interpretation: The captured JSON-LD artifacts are empty arrays on the homepage and Glucare Plus product page at desktop and mobile viewports.
limitations: Only JSON-LD was tested; this does not rule out other structured data formats.

title: Mobile lab captures show LCP above the checklist threshold on sampled pages
observation: The mobile LAB artifact records LCP 20,456 ms on the homepage, 19,952 ms on /benh-ly, and 18,956 ms on the diabetes-health article listing; the checklist target is under 2.5 seconds.

impact.user: Slow observed rendering can delay access to product and health information.
impact.business: Long wait times may interrupt discovery and evaluation.
impact.seo: The sampled LAB values exceed the stated performance target.
impact.technical: The measured LCP values are 7.6 to 8.2 times the 2,500 ms target.

suggested_direction: Profile and reduce the observed largest-contentful paint path, then repeat comparable mobile lab runs.
unknowns: These are single audit-browser LAB observations, not field Core Web Vitals or PageSpeed Insights scores; all page collections remain partial.
specialist_interpretation: The mobile LAB artifact records LCP 20,456 ms on the homepage, 19,952 ms on /benh-ly, and 18,956 ms on the diabetes-health article listing; the checklist target is under 2.5 seconds.

title: Viên An Đường combo URL promotion and displayed pack count disagree
